I'm not sure what you want to draw, or what medium you want to use. I'd recommend starting in pencil. It's easy to erase and inexpensive to buy.

As for what to draw... when I was in art classes in high school, my instructor took a roll of white paper towels and other various items (mostly books, I think) and wrapped them in white paper. This helps you see shadows really well. Shadows contrast nicely against the white surfaces. Also, if you're going to try this, place everything on a white piece of poster board or a large sheet of white paper. If you're using natural light and don't complete the drawing in one day (which is fine), make sure to draw at a similar time of day, as the shadows will change with the angle of the sun. If you're using a lamp as a light source, then draw whenever you please.

However, if you're wanting to do cartoons or animation or similar styles, this could still help, but likely not as much.

I found the hardest part of learning to draw was teaching my brain to see things properly. Once you look at something the way you need to, getting it on paper becomes easy.
